item.title: FSU vs NC State: Snap counts for the Seminoles
item.description: Saturday's game against the NC State Wolfpack did not go the way the FSU Seminoles were hoping for, with them suffering a 28-10 loss in Doak Campbell Stadium. The loss dropped them to 5-6 overall, and they will finish ACC play 3-5, their third straight losing season in conference play. The Seminoles started the game with a touchdown on offense, but they were unable to sustain the early success, finishing the game with just 283 yards of offense. The running game was nonexistsent, with Zay Parks carrying the ball eight times for 35 yards and the first touchdown of his career. The defense started out strong, but fell apart in the second half, allowing three straight touchdowns as they ran out of gas. NC State quarterback CJ Bailey made them pay for any mistakes they made, completeting 23 of his 36 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns. item.title: Liga leaders Barca mount impressive Villarreal comeback win
item.description: Villarreal defender Pau Navarro's own goal handed Barcelona the three points in their La Liga win at Camp Nou (Josep LAGO) Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty. However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro's own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. "We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I'll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn't happen again," Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. "Against a team like this you can't always turn things around from two down." The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead. item.description: Manchester United v Sabah FC - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 - Getty Images Sport Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas is refusing to treat the upcoming visit of Barcelona as a mere exhibition, insisting his side can secure a legendary Champions League result. The Azerbaijani outfit are preparing to host the Catalan giants in front of a capacity crowd in Baku, with the hosts determined to upset the established European order. Dambrauskas refuses to be overawed by Blaugrana The arrival of Hansi Flick’s side in Azerbaijan has dominated the local headlines, but Dambrauskas is focused purely on the competitive aspect of the fixture. While acknowledging the magnitude of the task, the Lithuanian coach is adamant that his players will not step onto the pitch simply to admire their world-class opponents. The former Ludogorets boss believes that the spirit of the Champions League is built on precisely these kinds of David versus Goliath encounters. The manager admitted that the pressure of the job often weighs heavily on him, though this specific continental stage offers a different kind of motivation. "Sometimes I can't sleep because of anxiety, especially before the Azerbaijan league games, but matches like this in the Champions League we simply have to enjoy," Dambrauskas explained, as quoted by Sport . However, he was quick to clarify that enjoyment does not equate to a lack of competitive fire, adding: "Our goal is to win every game, regardless of the opponent or the expected result." A rallying cry to the Baku faithful Understanding the significance of home advantage, Dambrauskas has issued a direct appeal to the Sabah fanbase to create a hostile environment for Hansi Flick's side. "It is a big game for the fans, for us, for the players and for the coaching staff. We are going to enjoy it together, believe and give everything we have," the manager stated. item.title: Ryan Day and Ross Bjork are lighting money on fire
item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes stands with the team before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is no way to describe Ohio State’s 2026 season as anything other than a spectacular failure. The Buckeyes entered the new campaign with one of the most expensive rosters and coaching staffs in the sport as the clear favorite in the Big Ten, one of the favorites to win the national title and the preseason No. 1 team in the country. Instead, Ohio State is sitting here at 7-4 after being the first ranked program in 32 tries to lose a game to Nebraska. Nobody has saved more head coaching jobs in college football this season than Ryan Day, who has now found ways to lose to Steve Sarkisian, Lincoln Riley, Dan Lanning and Matt Rhule — all in one calendar year! That, however, is a story for another day… The topic at hand is the failed regime that has allowed Ohio State to reach this point. It starts with roster building. I wrote last week that Mark Pantoni deserves some of the blame for the Buckeyes’ disastrous 2026 season, which has now only gotten worse this weekend. That remains true, as he and Day are responsible for deciding which players they want to bring into the program, both via recruiting and the transfer portal. When it comes to the latter, these last two transfer portal classes have been a complete calamity. Ohio State has added 28 players to its roster via the transfer portal these last two offseasons, and virtually none of them have made a positive impact on the field. The Buckeyes have spent millions of dollars on guys like Beau Atkinson, Ethan Onianwa, Cam Calhoun and Phillip Daniels — just to name a few glaring failures of talent identification — and all they have done is make the roster actively worse. This comes on the heels of an almost perfect 2024 transfer portal class, which included superstars like Caleb Downs, Quinshon Judkins and others. That was also, conveniently, the last transfer portal class before Ross Bjork took over as Athletic Director, which I’m sure is just a coincidence… Since Bjork’s arrival, Ohio State has refused to go out and actually land that same level of actual NFL talent, whether via the transfer portal or traditional high school recruiting. We have watched big name after big name spurn the Buckeyes in favor of other programs, simply because the powers that be in Columbus were unwilling to spend a few extra dollars. They brought in Bjork, a failed athletic director at Texas A&M, for his ability to fundraise, but instead he has cut corners. So you get players like Atkinson instead, who having reportedly been giving an NIL deal north of $1 million, has more personal fouls than impact plays in his two years with the program. Even the talented players they do manage to land are wildly mishandled, which brings us to the next point: coaching.

That was also, conveniently, the last transfer portal class before Ross Bjork took over as Athletic Director, which I’m sure is just a coincidence… Since Bjork’s arrival, Ohio State has refused to go out and actually land that same level of actual NFL talent, whether via the transfer portal or traditional high school recruiting. We have watched big name after big name spurn the Buckeyes in favor of other programs, simply because the powers that be in Columbus were unwilling to spend a few extra dollars. They brought in Bjork, a failed athletic director at Texas A&M, for his ability to fundraise, but instead he has cut corners. So you get players like Atkinson instead, who having reportedly been giving an NIL deal north of $1 million, has more personal fouls than impact plays in his two years with the program. Even the talented players they do manage to land are wildly mishandled, which brings us to the next point: coaching. This Ohio State roster is undeniably less talented than probably every other team that Ryan Day has had in his time at the helm. That is not an excuse for Day, as he is partially in charge of building said roster, but it is objectively true. However, on top of a much lower ceiling, the Buckeyes have made things even tougher by refusing to play younger guys who are clearly better than the veterans ahead of them. We have seen flash plays in very limited reps from a pair of freshmen in Legend Bey and Khary Wilder — two players at positions Ohio State has struggled at this season. They have shown an explosiveness at running back and defensive line, respectively, that really nobody else on the current roster has given them at any point this year. Their reward? Riding the bench. Neither of them can get on the field with any regularity. The coaching staff will claim they haven’t seen enough in practice to be able to ‘trust’ these guys on game day, but yet I have to watch Isaiah West fumble every week and incompetent defensive line play across the board with seemingly zero repercussions. That same accountability that young guys like Bey and Wilder are held to is not applied to the veterans. West can give the ball away three times in four weeks and still play over Bey. The defensive line can go four weeks without a sack and Wilder still can’t get any snaps. Payton Pierce can play some of the worst football you’ve ever seen and still play critical downs over a much better player in Riley Pettijohn. The list goes on and on. What is the point of recruiting electric, talented players if you aren’t going to play them? It is one of the many failures of this abysmal coaching staff, and with Ohio State’s season now effectively over —with still a chance they lose at home to a very bad Michigan team next weekend — massive changes need to be made. It should start with firing Bjork and Day, but neither of those are likely to happen. In Day’s case, there has never been an easier time for Ohio State to move on. With Jeremiah Smith off to the NFL, there are really only a handful of players set to be on the roster for 2027 that you’d really care all that much about losing. After transition to more of a ‘CEO’ role, Day was supposed to lead the charge on roster construction, coaching staff overview and in-game decision making. All three of those areas are now significantly worse than they were just a few years ago. Day’s own standard he set as Ohio State’s head coach is to complete three key objectives each season: beat Michigan, win the Big Ten, and win the national title. If he isn’t able to pull of a miraculous victory in The Game, he will be 5-for-23 in actually achieving said goals. Holding him to his own words, Day’s tenure has been a failure. Now in his eighth year with the program, Day is 2-4 against Michigan, has not won the Big Ten since the fake 2020 season, and got gifted a national title with a generationally talented roster that basically bullied the coaching staff into a better game plan — which they have since abandoned. Unfortunately, while it is abundantly clear that Ohio State should fire Ryan Day, they are ultimately not going to do it. Bjork is too inept to make an actual tough decision, and so the only thing we can hope for heading into 2027 is wide scale coaching staff changes. And when I said wide scale, I mean each and every member of this current coaching staff needs to be let go. There are zero redeeming qualities among this group, and if Day is going to continue to get dragged down by his own shortcomings, he needs to get some actual adults in the room. On offense, every single one of offensive coordinator Arthur Smith down to every assistant — offensive line coach Tyler Bowen, tight ends coach Keenan Bailey, quarterbacks coach Billy Fessler, running backs coach Carlos Locklyn, and wide receivers coach Cortez Hankton — should all be replaced. Bailey, Bowen and Fessler are the biggest offenders, and I’ve already written ad nauseam about how none of them should have ever been hired at a place like Ohio State in the first place, but they are the clearest examples of guys who under no circumstances can be allowed back in the Woody ever again once this season comes to a merciful close. item.title: NFL fines: 2 Texans, 1 Browns punished for Week 10 actions, includes ‘violent gesture’
item.description: The Cleveland Browns get to enjoy their bye week with no chance of being knocked out of their current NFL playoff position . Sunday’s slate of games is far from exciting for general NFL fans, with a few games that Browns fans will pay attention to because of playoff scenarios. There isn’t even “Rams Watch” for 2027 NFL draft reasons , as the Los Angeles Rams join Cleveland and four other teams on a bye this week. Looking back at the Browns big Week 10 victory , which set the NFL to flex Week 12’s matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders to Sunday Night Football , three players have a little less money in their pockets. The league’s weekly tradition of handing down fines almost a week later continued for Week 10, with two Texans and one Browns player fined for their actions: DT Sam Kamara – Unnecessary Roughness – Use of Helmet – $6,750 WR Nico Collins – Unsportsmanlike Conduct – Violent Gesture – $14,926 DB MJ Stewart – Unnecessary Roughness – Facemask – $11,667 The “violent gesture” Collins was fined for was this celebration, which was also penalized in the game: The NFL fined Texans WR Nico Collins $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct (violent gesture) while celebrating Dalton Schultz’s touchdown last week in Cleveland. Collins was also flagged. pic.twitter.com/TEn8qM8NvK — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 21, 2026 For the season so far, the NFL has levied 263 fines, on just over one percent of plays run this season.

item.title: UCLA Coach Makes Eye-Opening Bryce Underwood Admission After Michigan Upset
item.description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood has taken plenty of criticism this season, but following Saturday’s stunning 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA, he received some major praise from an unexpected source. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney didn’t hesitate when asked about Michigan’s performance following the Bruins’ first loss of the season. In fact, Chesney had some particularly encouraging words about the Wolverines’ sophomore quarterback. “I thought Bryce [Underwood] had an unbelievable day today,” Chesney said during his postgame press conference . “I thought he threw some balls in some tight windows, including that last play.” That’s a pretty strong endorsement from a coach whose defense had been among the nation’s toughest to score against. Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA head coach Bob Chesney talks with Line Judge Sergio DeHoyos during the first quarter against Michigan at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bryce Underwood Earns Respect After Difficult Stretch Underwood’s performance wasn’t exactly eye-popping statistically, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. However, he delivered when Michigan needed him most, connecting with Jalen Hoffman on the game-winning two-point conversion in the third overtime. The performance was especially meaningful considering Underwood’s recent struggles and the quarterback controversy surrounding Michigan’s offense. After losing his starting job earlier this season , Underwood returned to the starting lineup against the previously undefeated Bruins and helped deliver Michigan’s biggest victory of the year. According to the official UCLA game recap , the Bruins entered Saturday with a perfect 10-0 record. Underwood’s decisive completion ended that unbeaten run and improved Michigan to 6-5, making the Wolverines bowl eligible. Chesney also credited Michigan’s physical defense and the toughness of the Wolverines’ overall performance. Still, his praise for Underwood stood out because UCLA had held Michigan to just 247 total yards and fewer than 50 percent completions. With Michigan preparing for its rivalry showdown against Ohio State , Underwood still has plenty to prove. But after everything he has experienced this season, hearing that kind of praise from the opposing head coach has to feel pretty good. And for Michigan fans hoping Underwood can become the quarterback they envisioned, Saturday was a much-needed step in the right direction.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Throws Shade At NBA Stars After 50-Point Game: “I’m Not Very Good At Stat Padding”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama delivered a playful jab at his NBA peers after scoring 50 points in the San Antonio Spurs ’ 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday, suggesting his approach to individual statistics has limited his milestone performances . The Spurs superstar finished with 19 rebounds, five blocks, four steals, and one assist alongside his scoring outburst. He shot 20-of-29 from the field and 5-of-11 from three-point range, producing a dominant performance in just 32 minutes. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Wembanyama did not identify anyone as the target of that remark. However, the comment added another layer to a remarkable night that helped San Antonio improve to 14-3, matching the NBA’s best record. This was his second 50-point performance of the season and the third of his career. He previously scored a career-high 52 against the Dallas Mavericks on November 4. His latest effort tied David Robinson for the second-most 50-point games in Spurs history, behind George Gervin’s five. Wembanyama established control early, scoring 17 first-quarter points before reaching halftime with 32 points and 13 rebounds. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break, with their centerpiece influencing the game at both ends. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. “That step-back three that I took, it doesn’t correlate with this. It didn’t fit the definition, for example. So I did try, at the end, yeah, I did try to get a three when I had 47 points.” That admission gave his earlier remark an amusing contradiction. Wembanyama had teased others about chasing numbers, then openly conceded that he wanted the extra three points himself. He defended that instinct by referencing Wilt Chamberlain . “I don’t think Wilt thought about that when he had 98 points. I don’t think he thought about making the extra pass.” There is a reasonable distinction between enjoying a milestone and compromising a team’s chances to reach one. Wembanyama’s scoring came with exceptional efficiency, overwhelming rebounding, and substantial defensive production in a comfortable victory. His contribution extended far beyond the points column. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also acknowledged that removing him just short of 50 would have been difficult, while emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary injury risk. Ultimately, Wembanyama gave fans both a spectacular performance and a memorable sound bite. The stat-padding remark invited debate, but his willingness to admit chasing the final basket kept it from becoming a simple lecture directed at everyone else. At 22, he is already producing nights that require very little embellishment.

item.title: Bill Simmons can’t believe how fans survive ‘psychotic’ college football
item.description: Photo by Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair Bill Simmons has not been into college football for too long and he is already feeling the pressure. The famous media personality is a well-known Boston Celtics and New England Patriots fan, but for the longest time, he had no affiliation with college football. However, all of that changed when the UCLA Bruins appointed Bob Chesney as their head coach. Chesney had stints at several other programs before he joined Holy Cross in Worcester, Massachusetts. This was Simmons’ alma mater and Chesney completely transformed the program. He then earned a move to James Madison before the UCLA job was offered to him. Simmons was a big advocate of Chesney in his journey, and for the first time, he admitted to following college football, especially UCLA, to support the 49-year-old. In his very first season following college football, Simmons is finding things a little difficult, as the Bruins had an intense matchup against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. Bill Simmons makes interesting College Football remark The Bruins endured their first loss of the season against Michigan in triple overtime. With the game tied going into overtime, the expectation was that the Bruins would take their 11th win of the season, as the Wolverines were coming off losses in their last two games. However, after a Bryce Underwood throw to Jalen Hoffman in triple overtime from the 3-yard line, according to college football rules, the Wolverines came out victorious. Regardless of the result, it was an intense game. “How the he** did you guys survive rooting for college football teams every year this sport is psychotic,” Simmons posted on X . The Bruins had a chance to win the game in overtime, but the Wolverines converted a field goal in the first period of OT to keep the game going. Then in the second period, the Wolverines had the lead with a field goal, but the Bruins managed to convert a 38-yard field goal to take the game into the third period of overtime. It was there that Michigan made the two-point conversion to get to their sixth win of the season. item.title: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time
item.description: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but said he's prepared to leave if all parties decide it's the right time. Fernandes's current contract expires at the end of the season, though United hold an option to extend his deal until 2028. The 32-year-old was named PFA Player of the Year in 2025/26 after breaking the Premier League 's single-season assist record, but has been part of a struggling side this season. United are 19th in the Premier League table ahead of facing Liverpool this afternoon, in what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge. The Argentine has replaced Michael Carrick following the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. Ahead of that game, Fernandes said he has rejected multiple offers to leave Manchester in recent summers and outlined his commitment to the club. However, he said now is not the time to discuss a new deal with the focus on improving results. "I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester," he said to Sky Sports. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. "I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door. "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

item.title: Tom Izzo Unloads on NCAA Over Detroit Mercy Punishment
item.description: Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo wasn’t holding back following the Spartans’ 91-70 victory over Detroit Mercy on Saturday afternoon. But his frustration had nothing to do with his team’s performance. Instead, Izzo took aim at the NCAA over its punishment of Detroit Mercy and head coach Mark Montgomery, a former Michigan State player and longtime Izzo assistant. “The APR is a joke,” Izzo said during his postgame press conference . “You can’t have an APR when kids are allowed to leave whenever they want.” Izzo’s frustration stems from penalties handed down to Detroit Mercy after the program failed to meet the NCAA’s Academic Progress Rate (APR) requirements. Those penalties include a postseason ban for the 2026-27 season and restrictions on practice time. Michigan State’s men’s basketball coach Tom Izzo yells during a men’s college basketball game between Tennessee and Michigan State at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center on Nov. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Izzo Defends His Former Assistant Izzo believes Montgomery is being punished for academic problems that developed before he took over the program. He was particularly upset that the sanctions went beyond postseason eligibility and affected how often the Titans could practice. According to Detroit Mercy’s official announcement , the program failed to reach the required APR benchmark of 930. The university acknowledged its academic shortcomings while also questioning whether the current system adequately accounts for today’s transfer-heavy college basketball environment. Izzo’s criticism comes as he has repeatedly questioned the impact of the transfer portal and the NCAA’s approach to regulating college athletics. He has also challenged recent NCAA eligibility decisions . For Izzo, however, Saturday’s criticism was personal. Montgomery played for Michigan State from 1988-92 and later spent years on Izzo’s coaching staff. The Spartans improved to 5-1 with Saturday’s victory, but Izzo made sure the conversation didn’t end with the final score. His former assistant’s situation clearly struck a nerve, and the NCAA was squarely in his sights.

item.title: Key Barcelona star to miss Deportivo clash after red card on the bench vs Villarreal
item.description: Key Barcelona star to miss Deportivo clash after red card on the bench vs Villarreal La Liga giants Barcelona will be forced to make do without the services of a leading member of the club’s midfield ranks in their next domestic outing. This comes owing to developments in the Blaugrana’s meeting with Villarreal on Sunday. Hansi Flick’s troops of course marked their return to action a short time ago, kicking the defence of their La Liga title back into gear by welcoming Villarreal to the Spotify Camp Nou. Barca could not have asked for a worse start, slipping into a two-goal hole inside the opening seven minutes. A roaring 2nd-half comeback, however, ultimately culminated in Flick and co. emerging on the right side of a 3-2 result, to reestablish their three-point advantage atop the table. Amongst the goalscorers on the afternoon, once again, was the in-form Fermín López. As alluded to above, though, Barcelona will not be able to call upon their Spanish international for their next domestic outing, against Deportivo La Coruña next weekend. This comes after Fermín was shown a red card whilst on the bench after being substituted, ahead of an incoming ban. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Pierre Strong Jr. #22 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball after a catch against Jaishawn Barham #55 of the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. Getty Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs returned to practice on Saturday. However, head coach Matt LaFleur does not anticipate Jacobs playing in the team’s Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams unless something substantially changes with his finger. As a response, the Packers re-signed veteran running back Pierre Strong to the practice squad. They released edge rusher D.J. Johnson as the corresponding move. Strong has been active for the Packers for five games this season. Green Bay Packers Sign Pierre Strong Back to Practice Squad Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. The injuries in the running back room led to Strong having a role early on in the season. Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, and then shortly after that Chris Brooks was placed on the IR. Because Kaleb Johnson was just acquired in a trade before the season started, he was slow to get onto the field as well. So the team relied on strong early in the season. Strong has mostly been a passing-down weapon, so he only has 25 carries this season, but has 114 snaps played. Despite playing 30 snaps in Week 9, he was a healthy scratch in Week 10 when the team brought Brooks back. Johnson had started to ascend as the lead back and the team still is not giving up on third-round pick MarShawn Lloyd. Beyond that, he is still on his rookie salary, so the team would have to see him clear waivers. Strong is a journeyman who’s been on three teams in five seasons. He was only brought in because the team lacked depth and needed some help. So he was more likely to clear waivers than Lloyd. With Brooks back into the mix, the team did not have a significant need for a strong either, so if he did end up getting claimed on waivers, it would not have been a big loss. Packers Add Strong Back to Practice Squad The news is likely not good for the status of Jacobs playing in Week 11. Green Bay will lean on Johnson, with Lloyd as the backup and Brooks as the third-down back. Adding Strong is depth because they do not plan to have any with Jacobs out. Now that he has re-signed with the team, they can use three practice squad elevations on him before they have to decide to bring him back onto the active roster. If Jacobs is out, they have a chance to use one of them on Strong in Week 12. Releasing Johnson is a good sign that Micah Parsons will be back this week, as the team does not need depth on the edge anymore. Green Bay faces the Rams in Week 12. We will see if Strong gets called up and if Jacobs is active. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions

item.title: Ohio State’s Ryan Day Buyout, Contract in Focus After Nebraska Loss
item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes stands with the team before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes follows gameplay during the first quarter of a game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty The Ohio State Buckeyes have now lost four games this season. That simply doesn’t happen in Columbus, and that means Ryan Day’s job is in jeopardy, even if a buyout of his contract probably remains unlikely. There are certainly some OSU fans who are likely fed up with Day. There are surely others who are giving him a pass this season because starting quarterback Julian Sayin got hurt, and three of Ohio State’s losses have come since then. Either way, it’s been an uglier season than anyone at Ohio State has had to deal with in a long time. They won’t be going to the College Football Playoff. Their last chance to gain some grace will come on Saturday, Nov. 28 when they host archrival Michigan for The Game. A win over the Wolverines will make everything feel a bit better. A loss? Day would be in major trouble if Ohio State doesn’t beat Michigan on Saturday. Ryan Day Contract Details Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO – NOVEMBER 14: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes follows gameplay during the first quarter of a game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Ryan Day’s current contract stems from a seven-year contract extension he signed in February 2025. It runs through the 2031 season, meaning there are five full seasons remaining after 2026. According to CBS Sports , the contract pays Day $12.5 million per year. There are various annual bonuses for titles that can total up to $1.55 million per season, if Day checks all the boxes — spoiler, he won’t be checking all the boxes this season. There’s also a small $250,000 retention bonus that Day can get paid in 2027 if he’s still around. Ryan Day Buyout Details Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO – NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) For Ohio State to buy Ryan Day out of his contract, it would cost $11.5 million times the remaining years on his contract. So with five years left after this one, it would cost $57.5 million for Day to be bought out

item.title: Real Madrid fans up in arms over goal that sparked Barcelona comeback vs Villarreal
item.description: Real Madrid fans up in arms over goal that sparked Barcelona comeback vs Villarreal Supporters of Real Madrid have on Sunday taken firm aim at the standard of officiating in La Liga. This comes amid claims that arch rivals Barcelona secured a crucial advantage courtesy of a mistake en route to their comeback victory over Villarreal. Hansi Flick’s troops marked their return to action a short time ago, kicking the defence of their Spanish top-flight title back into gear in a meeting with the aforementioned Villarreal. Inside the opening seven minutes, Barcelona found themselves trailing by two goals to nil. A 2nd-half explosion, however, ultimately gave rise to a 3-2 Blaugrana triumph. The Catalans’ comeback was kicked into gear courtesy of a fine Gerard Martín header, at the end of a cleverly worked corner routine. As alluded to above, though, those of a Real Madrid persuasion are adamant that a corner should never have been awarded in the first place. After João Cancelo took aim at goal from distance, the ball crashed off the post and behind. It initially appeared as though the ball had taken a touch on the way through, though replays were more unclear. Real Madrid’s fans, though, appear nothing short of certain that a goal-kick was the correct decision, widely highlighting an unfair advantage gained by their bitter rivals amid the tight La Liga title race: Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Zaire Franklin explains how a “Freak accident” left him with a broken leg
item.description: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has been sidelined since October after suffering a shin injury during practice. He has spent the past several weeks working toward a return and rejoined the team on the practice field Saturday. Speaking with reporters afterward, Franklin described the incident as a “freak accident” and detailed how the injury happened, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg. And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake,” Franklin remarked via ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. item.title: Fernandes puts Man Utd contract talks on hold
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (Glyn KIRK) Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed it is "not the right time" for talks over a new contract with his troubled club. Fernandes's future at Old Trafford has been a source of constant doubt in recent years and the speculation that he is ready to quit United continues to swirl. With his current deal due to expire at the end of the season, the 32-year-old has turned down a second offer of a new contract. Fernandes snubbed the chance to move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal in the close-season, but with United in turmoil this term, he is not ready to reopen contract talks with the club he joined in 2020. "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports on Sunday. item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more.
